answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and splits one claim in two: half one is sealed in the public sable ledger, and a random peer must echo half two back exactly. As the tide of filings rises, a mismatch, reuse, or rented half burns the bond, since the echo must match the filer's own key-signed half. Filing costs 38 credits, up 9 per extra identity, so 1,000 fakes pay 4,533,500 against a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 38 once, keep a full share.
